Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

do verb

for emphasis: I do like it; do come in

also does (for emphasis), did (for emphasis), I do!, do come in, so did I, so do I

classical

Ter. Ph. 1053–1054: Mē ad cēnam vocā. — Pol vērō vocō.
Cic. Fam. 14.4.1: ego vērō tē quam prīmum, mea vīta, cupiō vidēre

vērō

adverb, usually after the first word

indeed, truly (stressing the statement)

English stresses the auxiliary; Latin stresses the statement, with vērō or by repeating the verb (Dormiō, “I am asleep”). Facere can stand for a verb just used, as “do” does (Lewis & Short; et ego fēcī, “so did I”); but a short answer repeats the verb itself (see yes).

Other words

  • equidem — I for my part, I really

    adverb, mostly with the first person · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 378: Tibi equidem dīcō, manē.; Plaut. Most. 332–333c: nōlō equidem tē adflīgī

  • quīn (+ indicative) — do …! why don’t you …? (urging)

    interrogative adverb with the present indicative · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 1387: quid stās? quīn intrō īs?; Plaut. Asin. 597: quīn tū hīc manēs?

    The urging “do”: “do go in”, “do stay”. Lewis & Short: only in exhortation or remonstrance, never asking for a fact.

  • sānē (with an imperative) — do, by all means (granting)

    adverb · also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 971: Ī sānē

    (in this sense, vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.)

    Granting what was asked: “do go, then” (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Mē ad cēnam vocā. — Pol vērō vocō. — Eāmus intrō hinc. — Fīat.

    Invite me to dinner. — I do invite you! — Let’s go in. — Very well.Ter. Ph. 1053–1054

  • ego vērō tē quam prīmum, mea vīta, cupiō vidēre

    I do want to see you as soon as I can, my darlingCic. Fam. 14.4.1

  • Quid, taceam? quīn tū īs dormītum? — Dormiō, nē occlāmitēs.

    What, me be quiet? Why don’t you go to bed? — I am asleep: stop shouting.Plaut. Curc. 183–183b

  • Tibi equidem dīcō, manē.

    I am telling you: wait.Ter. Eun. 378

  • quid stās? quīn intrō īs?

    Why are you standing there? Do go in.Plaut. Mil. 1387

  • Ī sānē, et quantum potest parāta fac sint omnia.

    Do go, and get everything ready as fast as you can.Plaut. Amph. 971

  • et ego fēcī quī litterās Graecās senex didicī

    and so did I, who learnt Greek as an old manCic. Sen. 26

See also yes, is it …?, not.
